expectation: Nuclear stain in a subset of cells: naive and stem-like memory T cells. They should be scattered single cells in the lamina propria and clustered in lymphoid aggregates, on CD3E+ cells, with epithelium mostly negative.
observed: A has a broad haze and a few big blobs, with small bright dots scattered in the tissue and clusters at the aggregates. B and C show discrete bright dots on a hazy, dim epithelial ring. D shows round, nucleus-sized blobs. In E the cells are dense in the CD3E-rich aggregate and overlap the CD3E cells, but there are also many CD3E-negative cells.
why: Discrete nuclear-sized cells are enriched in the CD3E-dense aggregates, but contrast is low, with haze and some spread into partner-negative tissue.
